title: Identity-Paired Progressive Depth Training: When Trainability Persists Beyond Expressibility
authors: Athanasios Hadjidimoulas, Tirthak Patel, Anastasios Kyrillidis
abstract: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are a leading paradigm for near-term quantum computing, yet their training suffers from sensitivity to circuit depth, initialization, and landscape pathologies such as barren plateaus. We study \emph{progressive depth training} (PDT) -- a layerwise curriculum that trains a shallow circuit before appending new layers -- and identify a fundamental obstacle: fixed entangling gates (CNOTs) in hardware-efficient ansätze cause \emph{initialization shock}, an energy spike when new layers are added. We propose \emph{identity-paired progressive depth training} (IP-PDT), which appends forward/inverse block pairs -- each consisting of a standard rotation$+$CNOT block followed by its reverse -- that compose to the identity at initialization. Because the adjacent CNOT rings cancel, the effective circuit retains only \textit{a single entangling layer} surrounded by \textit{overparameterized local rotations}. We prove a simple \textit{Reachable Set Saturation Theorem}: under this construction the variational manifold expands exactly once (when post-entangler rotations are first introduced) and then \emph{saturates}; all subsequent depth increases provide pure overparameterization of single-qubit unitaries. Despite this saturation, progressive addition of rotation parameters can continue to improve optimization outcomes -- a phenomenon we term \emph{trainability beyond expressibility}. We formalize IP-PDT as a continuation method on nested manifolds, prove monotone energy guarantees under an acceptance rule, and connect energy error to ground-state fidelity through spectral-gap inequalities. A detailed resource analysis shows that IP-PDT achieves lower total gate cost than both baselines by eliminating most CNOT gates.
summary: This paper introduces Identity-Paired Progressive Depth Training (IP-PDT) to overcome training instabilities in Variational Quantum Algorithms. By strategically adding identity-paired blocks, it eliminates initialization shock while maintaining a trainable structure that allows optimization improvements beyond the point where the circuit's expressibility saturates. The work provides deep theoretical guarantees linking energy minimization to ground-state fidelity.
main_problem: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) suffer from training difficulties due to circuit depth sensitivity, initialization shock, and landscape pathologies like barren plateaus.
main_result: The proposed Identity-Paired Progressive Depth Training (IP-PDT) method eliminates initialization shock by appending identity-pair blocks, allowing optimization improvements to persist even after the variational manifold saturates ('trainability beyond expressibility').
method: The authors formalize IP-PDT as a homotopy continuation method on nested manifolds, proving monotone energy guarantees and bounding the difference between sequential minimizers using strong convexity arguments.
model_or_system: The study concerns VQAs minimizing an energy expectation $E(	heta) = \langle\psi(	heta)|H|\psi(	heta)angle$ for an n-qubit system, utilizing hardware-efficient ansätze built from single-qubit rotations and CNOT entangling layers.
key_observables: Energy expectation value ($E$), Ground-state fidelity ($F(\psi)$), Initialization Shock (energy spike upon depth increase).
important_parameters: Circuit depth ($D$), Jitter scale ($\sigma$), Strong convexity constant ($\mu_D$), Spectral gap ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis requires the jitter parameter $\sigma$ to be sufficiently small to maintain positive strong convexity across depth expansions.

paper_structure: The paper introduces PDT, proposes IP-PDT to solve initialization shock via CNOT cancellation, develops the theoretical framework using continuation methods, proves energy guarantees through strong convexity bounds, and finally connects energy error to ground-state fidelity.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (homotopy continuation, strong convexity analysis) to stabilize quantum circuit optimization protocols, which is crucial for developing reliable near-term quantum algorithms.
